2. The appellants in this case are seeking suspension of their sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.

3. The appellants have been convicted vide judgment Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.102 of 2024(3) dt.15-05-2024 dated 18.12.2023 and sentenced vide order dated 08.01.2024 passed by Radhe Singh @ Radhe Shyam Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120678945/

sentences.text: They have been ordered to suffer imprisonment for life with a fine of Rs. 50,000/- each for the offence under Section 364 IPC and in default of payment of fine, they shall further undergo six months rigorous imprisonment.

They have been further ordered to undergo imprisonment for life with a fine of Rs. 50,000/- each for the offence under Section 302 IPC and in default of payment of fine, they shall further undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months.

Further, they have to undergo rigorous imprisonment for five years and to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/- each and in default of payment of fine, they shall further undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months.
All the sentences are to run concurrently.

4. Learned senior counsel for the appellants submits that it is a case of blind murder in which at a much belated stage these appellants who are the co-sharer/agnates of the deceased have been falsely implicated.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.102 of 2024(3) dt.15-05-2024 5.
As per the prosecution story, the dead body of Shaktidhar Singh @ Mantu Singh was found in the railway station area.

The railway police registered a case of unnatural death vide U.D. Case No. 06 of 2009 dated 20.02.2009, got the postmortem of the dead body done and published the photograph of the deceased in the newspaper.

After the photograph was published, father of the deceased came,
identified the dead body and took away the same to his village where his last rites were performed.

6. Learned senior counsel submits that the postmortem report of the deceased was showing swelling and fracture in the head and it appeared that the deceased was assaulted by some hard and blunt substance.
The Investigating Officer of the case requested the Officer in-Charge of Rail Police Station, Sasaram to register it as a case of murder.

Accordingly, after about one and half month i.e.
on 06.04.2009 on the basis of the request of the S.I. of police, Rail Sasaram P.S. Case No. 11 of 2009 came to be registered under Sections 302 and 201 IPC.

entities.text: Rail Sasaram P.S. Case No. 11 of 2009
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 7. Learned senior counsel submits that in course of investigation, none of the prosecution witnesses came forward immediately to make a statement that they had seen the Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.102 of 2024(3) dt.15-05-2024 deceased in the company of these appellants on 19.02.2009 at about 9-9:30 P.M.
After about one month of the death of her husband, PW-4 lodged a case under Section 498A IPC against her in-laws and eleven persons including the appellants.
The appellants were granted anticipatory bail in the said case and, later on, the case was compromised.
In the said case under Section 498A IPC, the PW-4 did not whisper about the murder of her husband and no suspicion was raised against these appellants but
later on, she claimed that on 19.02.2009 Guddu Singh and Sunil Singh came to her house and asked her husband to accompany them to Tarachandi.
She wanted to accompany her husband but she was told to make her plan later.
She states thereafter, that at some distance from the house a Marcel vehicle was standing in which these two appellants were also sitting.

sentences.text: Learned senior counsel submits that in her evidence in course of trial, PW-4 has not at all stated about any motive behind the occurrence.

She has tried to develop the case on the theory of last seen but on perusal of the prosecution evidences, it would prima-facie appear that it is a case of no evidence much less a case of circumstantial evidence in which the criminological chain of the events are complete.
9. The prayer for bail of the appellants has been Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.102 of 2024(3)
dt.15-05-2024 opposed by Mr. Anil Singh, learned counsel for the informant.

Learned counsel has submitted that there was a property dispute, though, no material in this regard has come in course of trial but in this case, police had submitted a chargesheet implicating the father of the deceased also for hatching a conspiracy to kill his son.
The father of the deceased is no more.

10. It is submitted that there is no doubt that there is a delay of over few months in naming these appellants as the persons with whom the husband of the deceased had gone on 19.02.2009 but considering that PW-4 is a rustic lady of the village and she had no access to the court on her own,
the delay would not prove fatal.

11. Mr. Bipin Kumar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State has though opposed the prayer of the appellants but at the same time, on the query made by this Court as to whether the prosecution has suggested any property dispute as motive behind the occurrence, learned Additional Public Prosecutor informs that there is no such case of the prosecution.

12. We have considered the submissions made on behalf of the parties hereinabove and perused the records for prima-facie view for purpose of grant of suspension of sentence Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.102 of 2024(3) dt.15-05-2024 and release of the appellants on bail.
We find that the theory of last seen has emanated through the wife of the deceased (PW-4) at a much belated stage when her relationship got sour with her family members after death of her husband.
Even in her case lodged under Section 498A IPC on 24.03.2009, she did not whisper a word about any suspicion against the appellants in the murder of her husband.
The gap is too far and even motive is missing

,
therefore, at this stage we take a prima-facie view to direct suspension of sentence and release of the appellants on bail during the pendency of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-III, Rohtas at Sasaram in connection with S.Tr. No. 326 of 2012,
C.I.S. No. 1403 of 2013 arising out of Rail Sasaram P.S. Case No. 11 of 2009.
13.
